claims.statement: asynq runs in-process in the api-server and uses the same Redis instance as caching and the event bus; task type strings are stable contracts between the enqueue site and the handler.

Worker taxonomy covers disbursement (execute, poller, status inquiry, wallet settlement, IPN), bulk transfer (orchestration, 9Pay-specific, row worker, revenue transaction), recovery sweepers (verified_transfer_recovery, transfer_paid_amounts), attendance (auto-reject checkout, sweep, credit quota), BCC import, notifications (flexpay_salary_notification_worker, payroll_report_email_worker), and audit/import jobs (audit_log_write_worker, employee_import_worker, import_job_worker).

Workers are idempotent and rely on per-task idempotency keys (bulk_transfer_batches.enqueue_state, wallet_payments.txn_id, attendances.quota_credited_at, flexpay_salary_notifications.attempt plus lease model) so retries are not distinguishable from first attempts.

Multi-aggregate writes are wrapped in domain.TransactionManager.RunInTransaction; cache invalidation runs as an after-commit callback per ADR-007, and event publishing via Redis Streams is post-commit so a crash between commit and publish is recoverable from the outbox.
The scheduler (internal/app/services/scheduler/) runs in-process and enqueues scheduled tasks at the configured cadence; restarting the api-server reschedules based on the persisted schedule.

Workers log at critical junctions via slog (never fmt.Printf) per backend/AGENTS.md, emit Prometheus metrics through internal/infra/observability/, and the system-health and cron-health UI surfaces consume these signals.
